title: Monotonic Array
spaceBreakdown:
- bool inc, dec: constant → O(1)
- int i loop variable: constant → O(1)
- not counted: input vector nums
approach: An array is monotonic iff it does not contain both an increase and a decrease among its adjacent pairs (adjacent comparisons are sufficient because monotonicity is transitive). Do one left-to-right pass maintaining two booleans: `inc` (any nums[i] > nums[i-1] seen) and `dec` (any nums[i] < nums[i-1] seen). If both ever become true, return false immediately; otherwise return true. Equal adjacent values set neither flag, so all-equal arrays correctly return true.
hints: The definition quantifies over all pairs (i, j) with i ≤ j, but n can be 10^5. What smaller, local set of comparisons between adjacent elements is enough to decide the same property?
Single linear pass with two boolean flags. On [1,3,2]: pair 1→3 sets the "increase" flag, pair 3→2 sets the "decrease" flag; both flags true ⇒ not monotonic.

```
inc = false, dec = false
for i = 1 to n-1:
    if nums[i] > nums[i-1]: inc = true
    if nums[i] < nums[i-1]: dec = true
    if inc and dec: return false
return true
```

**Single element** - n = 1, no adjacent pairs exist.
`Input: nums = [5]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: looping from i = 0 and reading nums[i-1] → out-of-bounds read / wrong output

**All equal** - every adjacent pair is equal, so neither flag is set.
`Input: nums = [7,7,7,7]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: initializing inc = true, dec = true → returns false

**Non-strict increasing with a tie** - equal values must be allowed.
`Input: nums = [1,2,2,3]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: returning false whenever nums[i] == nums[i-1] → returns false at the 2,2 pair

**Negatives only** - values can be negative; direction still works.
`Input: nums = [-3,-2,-1]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: initializing a flag based on sign of nums[0] (e.g., assuming positive ⇒ increasing) → returns false

followUps.q: The array arrives as an unbounded stream you cannot store. Can you still decide monotonicity?
followUps.a: Yes. Keep only the previous element and the two booleans inc/dec. Each new element updates the flags against the stored previous value, then becomes the new previous. Time O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: Now require strictly monotonic (no equal adjacent values allowed). How does the check change?
followUps.a: Add a third condition: if nums[i] == nums[i-1], return false immediately. The inc/dec flags still detect a direction flip. Time O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: Instead of a yes/no answer, return the length of the longest contiguous monotonic subarray.
followUps.a: Use a sliding window expanding while the current pair keeps the same direction (or is equal); when the direction flips, shrink the left side past the previous index. Track the max window length. Time O(n), space O(1).
